thread.title: Wall Street Is Systematically Taking Down Market Leaders

author: Giovanni DiMauro
title: Wall Street Is Systematically Taking Down Market Leaders
text:
The game has changed; Wall Street is taking market leaders out to the woodshed for a good old fashion beating. Mr. Market is selling off this year's big winners with a vengeance. In the last two months, Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ), Alphabet ( GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ), and Nvidia ( NVDA ) along with many others have fallen into bear market territory.
I am not going to go into a huge fundamental analysis as this article is about the mood of the market and technical factors that have taken over control of these names for now.
All three of these stocks have been Wall Street darlings and with good reason. They are fantastic business models that have created a great deal of wealth for those lucky enough to hold through thick and thin over the last decade.
Is this sell off different? It feels like it, but to be frank, I do not know.
When in doubt, go to the charts.
Here is a 15-year weekly chart of Apple.
What an epic run! This stock may be one of the best wealth creation vehicles in human history. I only wish I would have been smart enough to buy Apple in 2003 when I bought my first iPod. I loved it and guess what? It still works.
Apple is my favorite stock of the four that I have listed for this article. The main problem here is the chart. This chart begs the computer algos to sell, sell, sell. Will the selling continue? No one knows for sure, what I do know is the market is dangerous and it will take out unhedged weak hands when least expected. The market can also destroy your hedge positions if not done properly.
Do not be fooled into thinking that the worst cannot happen, it often does and with regularity.
Here is an area that Apple could trade to over the next few weeks or months.
Is it too outlandish for a supercomputer program to trade Apple down to this level of $149? I think not, to my eye that doesn't even look like a line of solid support. Don't get me wrong, I am not even bearish on Apple, but I do believe the computer is going to find a way to get there. If $149 doesn't hold, then investors could see a quick trip to the next level of $119 in a huge bear market selloff.
We now live in a world of artificial intelligence and supercomputers. Why do you think these selloffs have become so much more violent? My answer: AI Computer algorithms.
Bull case for Apple In fairness to Apple, I believe they are one of the best run companies in the world. They have a ton of cash and they are making an absolute fortune off their service business.
I listened to the last earnings call and was blown away with the strength of their business model. $10B in service revenue for 90 days is a fascinating figure to this trader. The market is freaking out over them not reporting iPhone sales figures. I think the selloff is currently overdone, but that doesn't mean it can't take a quick trip down to $165.
The company will be buying back millions of shares nonstop, so I do not think it will trade to $119. I would be surprised to see $150, but one should remember that Apple was trading there in February of this year.
Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) has fallen off a cliff. Nvidia has been the premier gaming company of the last two years; the stock has been on a relentless tear. Momentum has changed, it appears the stock is now on a race to the bottom. This is all technical trading, Nvidia missed guidance top and bottom line and were punished mercilessly. When the market gets an earnings miss and it's game over, Nvidia is now likely to overshoot the downside.
Look at this 5-year chart.
Let's look at a 5-year weekly chart on GOOG.
Interested investors can see I drew two lines of possible support for Alphabet. The first is around $910 and the second is $775. Anyone considering taking a position needs to understand that the computers don't care what a great value GOOG is; AI could find a way to take the stock down to these levels.
Hedge funds blow up all the time, how does this happen? Margin trading, the world is trading on margin and it is dangerous. When traders get convicted and go on margin, they become very vulnerable. When all the market favorites take a plunge to the downside and you are on margin, it's game over.
I love Alphabet, I have Alexa in my house, I use Google every day and they are a great company. I want to buy the stock, but I will only buy longer term when I see $775. I understand this sounds extremely bearish, but once again, I am not totally bearish. I actually think we may be very near the end of this latest selloff and could go on a rally but, I do think GOOG will hit that level at some point in the next twelve months.
Let's take a look at my least favorite of the group, Facebook.
Facebook is under attack from the media and shareholders who are worried about government regulation and Facebook's public image. I drew four lines of support. Interested investors can see that two lines of support have been broken. Facebook needs to hold the current level or a drop to $115 is in the cards.
Last week, FB looked like they were holding up, what happened? I can tell you what I think happened; Hedges rolled off, traders felt bullish and did not have enough insurance and the market caught them naked today. Being naked long means you have no protection to the downside. If you are one of these people, I strongly caution you to consider using protection.
Facebook has been a great company and they still are, all three of these names listed are winners, they happen to be in a correction and no one knows where it is going to stop.
Conclusion High flying tech stocks are in correction, it is quick and painful when Wall Street darlings fall from grace. Is it over for these three goliaths? Not by a long shot, but it could get dicey over the coming weeks and months.
Investors need to understand that the market is in a correction, they are violent and unforgiving. In my view, it is important to understand that the game has changed, high priced momentum stocks are out of favor.
Pick your spots wisely and consider hedging any new positions, it is perfectly acceptable to have your stocks called away from you. While I think we could be setting up for a nice year-end rally, we could also be in the beginning of a prolonged bear market.
As always, do your own research and make your own decisions, do not be swayed by all the talking heads on Wall Street. Very few have any idea what will happen tomorrow.
I believe it is imperative to have an exit strategy before making any buying decisions, it can help you keep grounded in times of high volatility.
